text:
lina: Heads up — us-east1 dedicated pool just dropped ~~60%~~ of healthy GPUs over the last 2m. We're seeing queue growth and a bunch of 503s; routing started falling back to hosted automatically. Anyone on this?

sre-bot: ALERT us-east1-dedicated: healthy_nodes 48 -> 19 (2026-03-18T14:01:40Z). Eviction threshold hit, triggering fallback policy.

omar: seeing the same from infra metrics. Packet loss spike on nodepool-gpu-a around 14:00 UTC, then kubelet churn. Could be a NIC/flap event across the pool.

kai: checking NVidia driver logs now. quick grep shows repeated GPU reset errors on several hosts.

omar: i'm going to cordon and drain the most affected nodes (nodepool-gpu-a-0[3-7]) and restart the instances to reattach NICs. will bump weight to hosted to avoid error spikes during drains.

platform-oncall: executing weight shift to hosted (graceful) — posting command:
```
rictl traffic update --region us-east1 --weights '{"dedicated":0.25,"hosted":0.75}' --reason "emergency nodepool degradation"
```

kai: log excerpt from nodepool-gpu-a-05: 
```
[kubelet] E0320 14:00:12.345 kubelet.go:219] network plugin: failed to set up pod "abc" network: CNI failed: timed out
[nvidia] E0320 14:00:14.678 driver: GPU 0: GPU reset required, nvmlErrorUnknown
```

jen: hosted absorb will blow the cost run rate if this stays for >30m. Can we triage faster or put low-priority orgs to 0 while critical customers keep served?

lina: yes — let's throttle low-priority routes and keep high-priority pinned to dedicated where possible. Omar/Kai — estimate time to get nodes healthy?

omar: node restarts in progress — rolling 5 nodes now, each takes ~4-6m to boot and reattach NVMe/NIC. full heal estimate ~25-30m if no more flaps.

platform-oncall: setting org-level weights:
```
rictl org update-traffic --org low-priority --region us-east1 --dedicated-weight 0.0 --hosted-weight 1.0 --note "emergency spill to hosted"
rictl org update-traffic --org gold/customers --region us-east1 --dedicated-weight 1.0 --hosted-weight 0.0 --note "keep on dedicated"
```

jen: thanks — please add cost tag and open a billing watch so finance sees the temporary spike. tag: incident=1865432100, reason=us-east1-dedicated-fallthrough.

kai: quick follow-up — looks like a firmware rollout we pushed last night modified NIC driver on nodepool-gpu-a; pattern matches. filing internal bug: INFRA-6321 and opening support ticket with vendor.

omar: nodes are coming back healthy: healthy_nodes 19 -> 41 now (partial), continuing roll. will keep hosted weight at 0.75 until we hit 90% healthy capacity for the pool.

lina: agreed. timeline: continue rolling, keep low-priority routed to hosted, monitor latency and cost. After 90% healthy, we will gradually shift weights back in 10% increments and watch SLA/latency. Kai — post root-cause once vendor replies.

sre-bot: UPDATE us-east1-dedicated: healthy_nodes 41 -> 46 (2026-03-18T14:32:40Z). Fallback still active; hosted weight 0.75.

omar: final note — disabled that NIC firmware rollout for remaining nodepools and added a 30m pause in the firmware pipeline. INFRA-6321 link: https://redwood.internal/issue/INFRA-6321

lina: post-incident actions: 1) CIDR-level network diagnostics to vendor, 2) add early-warning metric for concurrent GPU resets, 3) run tabletop for firmware rollout policy. I'll create the follow-up doc. Closing this thread when weights are back to pre-incident. :white_check_mark:
